title: Double gigs that left his chops numb
summary: Thomas describes working until 2 a.m. with Abernathy, then with Bailey until 11, plus matinees. He was exhausted but saving to leave Milwaukee.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: And you'd do that after you got through with Abernathy?
After I got through with Abernathy, we worked until two o'clock on Saturday night then I'd catch a cab and go to work for Burke Bailey until around 11 o'clock.
What sort of place was that?
There's a river in Milwaukee, is there?
Yeah, I guess there is. Yeah.

Milwaukee River, I guess it is. Well, the fellow had a place out there and he was a helluva guy. He devoted his ideas, and music and things. We worked there sometimes until in 12 o'clock and the day Sunday.
Well, how could your chops stand up to that sort of thing? At that time they would take it, would they?
Yeah, numb, man. They were numb.
I mean that was hard. I mean because when you would come to a four piece.
Yeah, they were numb. They were absolutely numb. But, with a certain amount of youth, you can bounce back. A
certain amount of knowledge of how to treat your body and your chops, you can make it because you want everybody to get what they're paying for.
Yes but I mean you had a (thought) from your chops, your body is still involved working those hours.

I was sick, really sick. during hot. We got over that. So we worked there until around 12 o'clock and then 2 o'clock or 3 in the afternoon was the time for the matinee performance at Eagle's Ballroom two bands, you know. So we got there and we played until 2 to 5. I got back, had a chance to take a bath, wash up and get myself clean and keep myself from being smelly, get my chops together then go back and work from 8 to 1. After 1 o'clock I go* back to (?.) place, you know. But I needed to do that because I wanted to leave Milwaukee. Milwaukee had gotten --- Stan, I have an idea. You know most of my life has been musical and when music dies, (?.) dies, I want to be the first to know. Not if anyone tells me, I want to feel that.
When you were doing this, when you were saving up some money to get out of there.
Yeah. Well, I had to and I wanted to go. That was around six weeks of that.
